nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of NiOx/C only show C (002) diffraction peaks, indicating amorphous NiOx clusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction patterns (XRD) of NiOx/C only show the C (002) diffraction peaks, indicating the NiOx clusters in all functionalized supports are amorphous (Figure S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show ID/IG ratio of 1.16 for NiOx/C vs 0.90 for bare acetylene black, indicating increased surface defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra reveal pronounced augmentation in the ratio of the D band to G band within NiOx/C (1.16) compared to bare acetylene black (0.90).

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area of NiOx/C is 59.9 m²/g compared to 66.8 m²/g for acetylene black.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Brunner-Emmet-Teller (BET) measurement shows that the specific surface area of NiOx/C and acetylene black (C) are 59.9 m²g and 66.8 m²g, respectively (Figure S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images show NiOx clusters ~1.1 nm with no significant size change after heat treatment; Pt-NiOx/C reveals cluster-cluster heterostructures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Figure 1b and Figure S4a-b) of NiOx/C ... indicate that the NiOx clusters have an average size of about 1.1 nm. ... Notably, as can be seen from the HAADF-STEM images of Pt-NiOx/C (Figure 1f and Figure S11a-b), apparent Pt-NiOx cluster-cluster heterostructures are formed.

Bright field TEM showing nanoparticle morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images confirm Pt clusters average size ~1.4 nm in Pt-NiOx/C catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images of the Pt-NiOx/C catalysts show that the average size of Pt clusters is ~1.4 nm (Figure 1e and inset, Figure S10).

properties.description: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image showing Pt nanoparticles on NiOx support with lattice fringes

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p3/2 at 856.0 eV for Ni²⁺; Pt 4f binding energy positively shifts in Pt-NiOx/C vs Pt/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peaks centered at 856.0 eV can be assigned to the Ni 2p3/2 for Ni²⁺. ... the binding energy of Pt 4f in Pt-NiOx/C shifts positively compared to that of Pt/C.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES confirms valence state variation of Ni species after annealing; pre-edge peak positions match XPS trends.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra (Figure 1c) confirm the variation of the valence state of Ni species after annealing under different atmospheres.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-O coordination number is 5.67 at 1.60 Å for NiOx/C, varying to 5.50 and 5.76 after H₂/Ar and air annealing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The coordination number of Ni-O in the first shell layer for NiOx/C at 1.60 Å is 5.67. The coordination number of Ni-O decreases to 5.50 and increases to 5.76 after annealing in H₂/Ar atmosphere and air.

properties.description: Extended X-ray Absorption Fine Structure Fourier Transform

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS determines Ni content 1.32 wt% and Pt content 5.20 wt% in Pt-NiOx/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The contents of Ni and Pt in Pt-NiOx/C are determined to be 1.32 wt% and 5.20 wt% by inductively coupled plasma mass spectroscopy (ICP-MS), respectively (Table S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge XANES shows higher white line intensities for Pt-NiOx/C than Pt/C, indicating increased Pt oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt-NiOx/C exhibit higher white line intensities than Pt/C in the Pt L3-edge XANES spectra ... indicating that the interaction at the heterostructure interface contributes to the increment of the average oxidation state of Pt.

properties.analysis: Pt L3 edge oxidation state analysis

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM elemental mapping confirms uniform Ni distribution in NiOx/C and presence of Pt-NiOx interfaces in Pt-NiOx/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The STEM elemental mapping of NiOx/C also clearly verifies the uniform distribution of Ni species across the carbon black particle (Figure S5). The elemental mapping images of Pt-NiOx/C firmly confirm the presence of a significant number of interfaces (Figure 1g).
